ordered_diagnoses: Relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder overlap

facts.raw_span: A 47-year-old Caucasian woman
23-year history of presumed multiple sclerosis
four episodes of optic neuritis since 1989
longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis in 1995
persistently negative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) oligoclonal bands
unremarkable brain MRI scans
subacute onset of expressive aphasia and right-sided hemiparesis
expressive language impairment and 3/5 strength in the right arm and leg
normal complete blood count and metabolic panel
large T2-hyperintense, tumefactive lesion in the left prefrontal white matter
serum aquaporin-4 antibody titre was 1:1000 by cell-based assay
no evidence of intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis, no oligoclonal bands, and a normal cell count
A 47-year-old Caucasian woman
23-year history of presumed multiple sclerosis
four episodes of optic neuritis since 1989
longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis in 1995
persistently negative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) oligoclonal bands
unremarkable brain MRI scans
subacute onset of expressive aphasia and right-sided hemiparesis
expressive language impairment and 3/5 strength in the right arm and leg
normal complete blood count and metabolic panel
large T2-hyperintense, tumefactive lesion in the left prefrontal white matter
serum aquaporin-4 antibody titre was 1:1000 by cell-based assay
no evidence of intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis, no oligoclonal bands, and a normal cell count

concepts.why: The patient's history of optic neuritis and longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, combined with the presence of a large T2-hyperintense lesion in the left prefrontal white matter and a high serum aquaporin-4 antibody titre, supports this diagnosis.

The patient's 23-year history of presumed multiple sclerosis, characterized by episodes of optic neuritis and a longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, initially suggests this diagnosis, although the lack of oligoclonal bands and the presence of aquaporin-4 antibodies argue against it.

The large T2-hyperintense, tumefactive lesion in the left prefrontal white matter could be consistent with a tumefactive multiple sclerosis lesion, although the patient's clinical presentation and laboratory findings are more suggestive of another diagnosis.

The subacute onset of expressive aphasia and right-sided hemiparesis, combined with the presence of a large T2-hyperintense lesion, could suggest ADEM, although the patient's history and laboratory findings are not typical for this diagnosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder overlap
concepts.why: The patient's history of presumed multiple sclerosis, combined with the presence of a high serum aquaporin-4 antibody titre and a large T2-hyperintense lesion, could suggest an overlap between relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
It explains the uncovered finding of persistently negative cerebrospinal fluid oligoclonal bands and no evidence of intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis.

rationales.F04: Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis is more typical of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
rationales.F05: Negative CSF oligoclonal bands are more typical of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
rationales.F10: Tumefactive lesions can be seen in both neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder and tumefactive multiple sclerosis.
rationales.F11: Serum aquaporin-4 antibody is a specific marker for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
rationales.F12: No evidence of intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis is more typical of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
